item.text: {"search_note":"I did not find strong 2024 primary-source evidence that Erdoğan personally dismantled oligarchic capture, prosecuted politically connected business elites, or made procurement authorities genuinely independent. The best positives are AML/CFT compliance and formal procurement language; the structural evidence on SOEs, procurement, and executive appointments still points the other way.","evidence":[{"title":"Jurisdictions under Increased Monitoring - June 2024","publisher":"FATF","date":"2024-06-28","url":"https://www.fatf-gafi.org/en/publications/High-risk-and-other-monitored-jurisdictions/increased-monitoring-june-2024.html","summary":"FATF said Türkiye made “significant progress” and was removed from increased monitoring after strengthening AML/CFT supervision, sanctions, beneficial-ownership rules, financial intelligence use, and money-laundering/terror-financing prosecutions. This is meaningful anti-corruption-adjacent reform, but it is technical and financial-integrity focused rather than a full assault on patronage networks.","question_ids":["5B.5","5B.3"]},{"title":"Republic of Türkiye: 2024 Article IV Consultation-Press Release; Staff Report; and Statement by the Executive Director for the Republic of Türkiye","publisher":"IMF","date":"2024-10-11","url":"https://www.imf.org/en/publications/cr/issues/2024/10/11/republic-of-trkiye-2024-article-iv-consultation-press-release-staff-report-and-statement-by-556139","summary":"IMF’s 2024 Article IV report says authorities made legal and regulatory updates to improve AML/CFT, including addressing shortcomings related to politically exposed persons, and notes a new anti-corruption strategy was being prepared.
